cases.rationale: A balanced-tree rewrite passed P1 equivalence, but the fixed Yosys 0.63/ABC generic mapping produced the same 100 gates and 18-gate longest topological path for baseline and candidate. Synthesis therefore handles the reassociation; the flow does not estimate placed timing or power, and review found no other defensible local change.

A depth-balanced five-input modular sum passed P1 equivalence. Baseline and candidate both mapped to 626 generic gates with a longest topological path of 68 gates, showing that the fixed synthesis flow removes the RTL grouping difference. No other whole-case optimization was identified.

Balancing the independent sum output passed P1 equivalence while preserving the selection logic. Both designs mapped to 340 generic gates with a 34-gate longest path. The case mux is already direct and exhaustive review found no additional PPA candidate, so the arithmetic rewrite is synthesis-handled.

Balancing the non-bypass arithmetic branch passed P1 equivalence. Baseline and candidate each mapped to 239 generic gates and a 35-gate longest path. The bypass priority is already minimal, so the fixed flow provides no measured basis for changing the module.

Factoring the common operand into a single source-level add passed P1 equivalence. ABC mapped both forms to 93 generic gates with a 31-gate longest path, demonstrating automatic common-logic handling in the fixed flow. The one-line module contains no further independent opportunity.

A case-based spelling that preserves the highest-index priority and valid behavior passed P1 equivalence. Baseline and candidate both mapped to 19 generic gates with a seven-gate longest path. The rewrite is synthesis-handled, and tree decoding would not preserve the required priority semantics.

A candidate retained the explicit eight-bit partial-sum truncation and only reassociated the subsequent modular additions. P1 equivalence passed, but both versions mapped to 107 generic gates with a 19-gate longest path. Widening across the partial boundary would change behavior, while the safe rewrite is synthesis-handled.

Fixed-width signed reassociation passed P1 bit-vector equivalence. Both forms mapped to 221 generic gates and a 34-gate longest path, so the fixed synthesis flow already handles grouping of this modular signed sum. No other logic exists in the case.

The four-input fixed-width sum is already expressed as a balanced two-level tree. Exhaustive review of the single expression found no lower-depth, behavior-preserving source transformation with an independent PPA mechanism.

Each sat_add call clamps its result before the next addition. Saturating addition is non-associative, so changing the call tree alters observable saturation points. The function implementation and invocation chain contain no redundant logic that can be safely removed.

The module is the canonical one-entry elastic register: readiness is asserted for an empty or consumed entry, valid updates on readiness, and payload updates only for accepted valid data. Exhaustive protocol review found no removable state or combinational level without changing reset or handshake behavior.

sum_q and valid_q are previous-cycle state, while c_i is consumed in the output stage on the current edge. Moving or reassociating arithmetic across that register boundary changes temporal alignment or latency. Each stage already contains one required addition, leaving no safe local PPA rewrite.

Review of the bypass, normal, optional-data, grant, and mask-update branches found no locally redundant cone. Selection is already delegated to a parallel-prefix leading-one primitive, and the mask state is required for fairness and stalled-request locking. The listed source is not independently measurable because its package, assertion, and selector dependencies are outside the case sources, but no defensible candidate was identified.

All three depth-specialized implementations were reviewed, including pass-through, singleton storage, reset suppression, secure duplication, normal pointer control, and optional zero output. Their apparent Boolean simplifications encode distinct clear, pass, or security behavior, and no bounded source change has a separate PPA mechanism. External counter, flop, package, and assertion dependencies preclude isolated whole-top measurement.

The two complementary counters, saturating arithmetic, simultaneous increment/decrement suppression, commit gating, fault-injection hook, and registered cross-sum integrity check were reviewed as one security mechanism. Sharing or deleting these apparently duplicated cones would weaken fault detection, while local Boolean respellings are synthesis-level transformations without a distinct PPA basis. Required package and prim_flop definitions are external to the case source.

Exhaustive review covered the pack and unpack elaboration branches, reset/clear sequencing, depth and pointer transitions, variable shifts, and ClearOnRead behavior. The shifts and counters implement the required width-ratio conversion, and removing their guards changes stale-data or handshake behavior. No isolated transformation with a defensible PPA hypothesis remained.

The complete assigned source is a compatibility wrapper that instantiates spill_register_flushable and ties flush_i low. Its remaining ports and parameters are direct pass-through connections, so there is no local datapath or control cone to optimize; the wrapped implementation is outside this case's source list.

The source is already a minimal one-entry stream register: one canonical ready equation, a payload enable for accepted valid input, and two load-enable flops with clear. Review found no redundant state or lower-depth control expression; the external macro only supplies the corresponding flop templates.

Review covered zero-depth/pass-through elaboration, arbitrary-depth pointer wrap, accepted push/pop accounting, simultaneous operations, fall-through forwarding, flush, and memory clock enable. The ordering of these controls is required for boundary cases, and straightforward case or enable refactoring is expected to collapse in synthesis without a distinct improvement mechanism. No behavior-safe candidate justified P2 work.

The degenerate, external/internal priority, lock, fair/unfair update, and non-power-of-two tree branches were all reviewed. Arbitration and payload selection are already logarithmic; fair next-state selection deliberately uses masked leading-zero counters, while unfair mode uses one bounded increment. A local rewrite would alter fairness/locking or duplicate established tree logic, and dependencies prevent isolated top measurement.

The complete implementation is the direct indexed data/valid mux plus a one-hot ready decode selected by the same index. No common expression, avoidable mux level, or state exists to remove; package and assertion dependencies do not conceal additional implementation in the assigned source.

All REG_TYPE branches were reviewed. Bypass is direct wiring, the simple buffer intentionally permits bubbles, and the skid buffer's output/temp state plus early-ready equation is required for full throughput with registered backpressure. Boolean respellings do not remove storage or handshake dependencies and have no separate fixed-flow PPA hypothesis.

The assigned source is a structural parameterized chain of axis_register stages with direct endpoint wiring. Every payload and handshake signal is required by the interface, and no local combinational or state logic exists independently of the instantiated stage implementation. The dependency is outside this case's listed sources.

Review covered every pipeline stage, zero-length bypass, circular output FIFO, half-full backpressure threshold, output prefetch, simultaneous enqueue/dequeue, and reset path. The registers and FIFO decouple the registered-ready pipeline from downstream stalls; removing or retiming them changes latency, capacity, or AXI-stream behavior. Constant-threshold and pointer expressions are already synthesis-recognizable, leaving no defensible source-level PPA candidate.
